correctness.rationale: The measure assumptions are verified explicitly: \(x^\beta dx\) is finite Radon and doubling on \([0,1]\), while \(\mu_\beta(B(0,r))/r^Q=r^{\beta+1-Q}/(\beta+1)\to0\). For \(\lambda>p+1\), adjacent weighted interval averages differ by \(O(h^{(\lambda-1)/p})\); subdivision forces equality because the exponent exceeds one, so every Campanato class is almost everywhere constant. For \(Q<\lambda\le p+1\), a power \(x^\delta\) with \(\max\{0,(\lambda-\beta-1)/p\}<\delta<(\lambda-Q)/p\) satisfies the Campanato bound in both endpoint and interior ball regimes but fails the required Hölder exponent at zero. All parameter intervals and the endpoint \(\lambda=p+1\) were checked symbolically.

value.rationale: The finding gives a negative answer to an explicit open question in a current primary source and explains the obstruction structurally rather than by a single isolated example. The exact threshold \(\lambda=p+1\) on a natural power-weighted interval separates an explicit nonembedding branch from a branch where the Campanato space collapses to constants. This also pinpoints why doubling alone cannot make the lower-regularity criterion global: local dimension can be strictly smaller than the endpoint dimension responsible for failure of lower \(Q\)-regularity.
